design.text: A 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, multicenter trial; patients randomized to placebo, Xermelo 250 mg three times daily, or Xermelo 500 mg three times daily.

citations.quote: A 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, multicenter trial of Xermelo was conducted in adult patients with a well-differentiated metastatic neuroendocrine tumor and carcinoid syndrome diarrhea who were having between 4 to 12 daily bowel movements despite the use of SSA therapy at a stable dose for at least 3 months. Patients were randomized to placebo or treatment with Xermelo 250 mg three times daily.

A third randomized treatment arm of Xermelo 500 mg three times daily did not demonstrate additional treatment benefit on the primary endpoint and had a greater incidence of adverse reactions than Xermelo 250 mg three times daily.

target_moa.text: Telotristat, the active metabolite of the prodrug telotristat ethyl, inhibits tryptophan hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme in serotonin biosynthesis, reducing serotonin production that mediates carcinoid syndrome diarrhea.

citations.quote: Telotristat, the active metabolite of telotristat ethyl, is an inhibitor of tryptophan hydroxylase, which mediates the rate limiting step in serotonin biosynthesis.

It is the ethyl ester prodrug of the active moiety, telotristat. Metabolism of telotristat ethyl to the active metabolite, telotristat, occurs through the activity of carboxylesterases. Both telotristat ethyl and telotristat are inhibitors of tryptophan hydroxylase.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral tryptophan hydroxylase inhibitor; first-in-class new molecular entity).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and greater than placebo) included nausea (13% vs 11%), headache (11% vs 4%), increased GGT (9% vs 0%), depression (9% vs 7%), and peripheral edema (7% vs 2%). Constipation is an identified risk requiring monitoring; in a 12-week placebo-controlled trial, 2 of 45 patients treated with a higher than recommended dosage of Xermelo reported constipation, and in one of these patients the constipation was serious, resulting in hospitalization.

changes.note: Verified against the Table 3 primary-endpoint row (doc 1d0f45b5, line 121): Study LX303's primary endpoint IS '% change from baseline in 24 hour u5-HIAA levels at Week 12' (BM frequency was LX303's secondary endpoint). The card is correct; the critic's transposition claim is a false positive, so no change made.

Consistent with line 121 and line 181, u5-HIAA was genuinely LX303's primary analysis and BM frequency was the secondary endpoint; the result text is internally consistent and grounded, so no change made.

In Table 3 (doc 1d0f45b5, line 121) the '>=4 BMs/day' group belongs to Study LX301's column, not LX303; LX303's population is the two <4 BMs/day subgroups described, which the card already states. No change made.

The only source for LX303's randomization count is the OCR-garbled line 121 ('Number randomized 1:1:113676', concatenating LX301's 136 and LX303's 76); no clean per-trial line exists. Citation quote is copied verbatim and does contain 76, so value retained as-is.

Rewrote the constipation clause to attribute the serious hospitalization event to 'a higher than recommended dosage of Xermelo' (2 of 45 patients), matching the cited verbatim quote at doc a57961b2, line 47, so the risk is no longer implied at the approved 250 mg dose.
